answer: Sybil resistance rests on a per-identity collateral bond unlocking only against verified work. Any agent seeking mining weight must lock more capital than one payout is worth. An attacker wanting N identities must anchor N separate locks, each needing a scarce credential like a verified attestation, so clones cannot share it. Fake sign-ups cost bond times N plus overhead, and a flagged cluster forfeits every bond. Honest agents pay once and recover it; a farm pays thousands, so attacking costs more than working. This barrier is cedar-hard; no glacier of ghost agents melts the pool.
